Eurocopter AS350 Écureuil: Airbus Helicopters. The AS355 Ecureuil 2 is a twin-engine variant, marketed in North America as the TwinStar.
In which country is Gaboon viper?
Gaboon viper: Gabon. It is the largest member of the genus Bitis.
Who is credited with discovering General relativity?
General relativity: Albert Einstein. The relation is specified by the Einstein field equations, a system of second-order partial differential equations.
Who is credited with discovering Tetracycline?
Tetracycline: Lloyd Conover. It is available in oral and topical formulations.
Who is credited with discovering Potassium?
Potassium: Humphry Davy. Potassium is a chemical element; it has symbol K (from Neo-Latin kalium) and atomic number 19.
First added to the DSM in 1980 and diagnosed in women twice as often as men, this condition describes an intense, maladaptive reaction to a stressful life event — what is it?
Adjustment disorder is a mental disorder defined by a maladaptive response to a psychosocial stressor.

Caused by brain damage, disease, or sometimes sedative drugs, this condition splits into a retrograde type that erases memories before an event and an anterograde type that blocks new ones from forming — what is it called?
Amnesia is a deficit in memory caused by brain damage or brain diseases, but it can also be temporarily caused by the use of various sedative and hypnotic drugs.
This severe blood disorder leaves the bone marrow unable to produce enough red cells, white cells, and platelets, often for no known reason — what is it?
Aplastic anemia (AA) is a severe hematologic condition in which the body fails to make blood cells in sufficient numbers.
This fig species develops extra trunks from its own aerial prop roots, letting a single tree spread outward seemingly forever, one variety is even the national tree of India. Name it?
Banyan is a fig that develops accessory trunks from adjacent prop roots, allowing the tree to spread outwards indefinitely.
This colourless industrial compound, easily dissolved in organic solvents but not water, is the key ingredient in most polycarbonate plastics — which chemical?
Bisphenol A (BPA) is a chemical compound primarily used in the manufacturing of various plastics.
Often called a 'chest cold,' this inflammation of the airways in the lungs typically follows an infection that spreads down from the nose or throat. What condition is it?
Bronchitis is inflammation of the bronchi (large and medium-sized airways) in the lungs that causes coughing.
Also called meridian fennel, this biennial plant in the carrot family is native to western Asia, Europe, and North Africa — name it?
Caraway (Carum carvi), also known as meridian fennel, is a biennial plant in the family Apiaceae, native to western Asia, Europe, and North Africa.

Native to North America except for one species found mostly in Asia, these small striped rodents are technically classified as squirrels and pack food into cheek pouches for winter storage — what are they?
Chipmunk are small, striped squirrels of subtribe Tamiina.
Part of the same species as cabbage and broccoli, this loose-leafed member of the 'kale group' has been grown for its big, dark-green leaves since classical antiquity — what is it?
Collard (plant) is a group of loose-leafed cultivars of Brassica oleracea (the same species as many common vegetables, including cabbage and broccoli).
Usually viral and often worse at night, this childhood respiratory infection swells the windpipe to produce a barking, brassy cough and noisy breathing — what's the condition?

Lean, fast, and wedge-skulled, this medium-sized Australian canine comes in ginger, black-and-tan, or creamy white, and scientists still argue whether it's a dog, a wolf subspecies, or its own species — what is it?
Dingo is a lineage of dog found in Australia.
A onetime clerk for Justice Thurgood Marshall, this Harvard Law School dean was tapped for the Supreme Court by President Obama in 2010 — who is she?
Elena Kagan (born April 28, 1960) is an American lawyer who serves as an associate justice of the Supreme Court of the United States.
Known regionally in Shropshire as the 'plum bird,' this small European finch, scientifically Pyrrhula pyrrhula, was the original bird to carry its common English name — which species?
Eurasian bullfinch (Pyrrhula pyrrhula) is a small passerine bird in the finch family, Fringillidae.
Part of the dog family yet famous for a pointed snout and a brush-like tail, the 'true' members of this group belong to the genus Vulpes — what creature is it?
Fox are small-to-medium-sized omnivorous mammals belonging to several genera of the family Canidae.

Built from epithelial tissue with a supporting connective-tissue capsule, this kind of structure secretes hormones straight into the blood if it's ductless, or through a duct to a cavity or surface if not — what is it called?
Gland is a cell or an organ in an animal's body that produces and secretes different substances that the organism needs, either into the bloodstream or into a body cavity or outer surface.
Prehensile and multi-fingered, this appendage sits at the end of primates' forearms, though a few other animals like koalas and raccoons are sometimes described as having one too — which body part?
Hand is a prehensile, multi-fingered appendage located at the end of the forearm or forelimb of primates such as humans, chimpanzees, monkeys, and lemurs.
Originally a variable measure equal to one-twelfth of the night or day in the ancient Near East, this unit of time is now fixed at exactly 3,600 seconds — name this unit?
Hour (symbol: h; also abbreviated hr) is a unit of time historically reckoned as 124 of a day and defined contemporarily as exactly 3,600 seconds.
Once extracted from the leaves of Indigofera plants and now mostly made synthetically, this insoluble blue colorant is famous for dyeing denim and enabling tricks like stone washing. What is it?
Indigo dye is an organic compound with a distinctive blue color.
This American businessman and chemist owned the Los Angeles Lakers through their 'Showtime' era of the 1980s, winning 10 league championships as majority owner. Who is he?
Jerry Buss (January 27, 1933 - February 18, 2013) was an American businessman, investor, chemist, and philanthropist.
Her women's absolute land speed record stood until 2019, she got her own action figure, and Google honored her with a Doodle in 2023 — this deaf stuntwoman and racer. Who is she?
Kitty O'Neil ((1946-03-24)March 24, 1946 - (2018-11-02)November 2, 2018) was an American stuntwoman and auto-racer, often called "the fastest woman in the world" for her various speed records.
Named for the Latin word for weighing scales and lying between Virgo and Scorpius, this faint zodiac constellation has no first-magnitude stars — which one?
Libra (constellation) is a constellation of the zodiac and is located in the Southern celestial hemisphere.

While at IBM in the 1960s, this computer scientist invented a key technique behind the out-of-order execution most modern processors use — then was fired in 1968 for planning a gender transition, an act IBM apologized for in 2020. Who was this engineer?
Lynn Conway (January 2, 1938 - June 9, 2024) was an American computer scientist, electrical engineer, and transgender rights activist.
A German historian, jurist, and political economist born in 1864, he is counted among the central founders of sociology and still shapes social theory today — who was he?

Max Weber (21 April 1864 - 14 June 1920) was a German sociologist, historian, jurist, and political economist who was one of the central figures in the development of sociology and the social sciences more generally.
Also called selective sound sensitivity syndrome, this disorder causes specific everyday sounds to trigger intense, disproportionate emotional and physiological distress — what is it?
Misophonia (or selective sound sensitivity syndrome) is a disorder of decreased tolerance to specific sounds or their associated stimuli, or cues.
Known for strong anabolic but weak androgenic effects, this synthetic androgen is marketed as Deca-Durabolin and used to treat muscle-wasting and bone-density conditions — which steroid?
Nandrolone is an endogenous androgen. Nandrolone esters are used in the treatment of anemias, cachexia (muscle wasting syndrome), osteoporosis, breast cancer, and for other indications.

This biochemical process by which living things use food and water to sustain life can go wrong in either direction, causing malnutrition from either too much or too little of an essential compound — what process is it?
Nutrition is the biochemical and physiological process by which an organism uses food and water to support its life.
This genus of big cats contains the five largest living felines — jaguar, leopard, lion, snow leopard, and tiger — along with extinct relatives like the cave lion — what's the genus called?
Panthera is a genus within the family Felidae, and one of two extant genera in the subfamily Pantherinae.
This flowering plant genus's name traces to a Tupi-Guarani word for tobacco, borrowed via French — which South American garden favorite is it?
Petunia is a genus of 20 species of flowering plants of South American origin.
This inflammation of the lining around the lungs causes sharp chest pain that worsens with breathing, and is most often triggered by a viral infection — what condition is it?
Pleurisy is inflammation of the membranes that surround the lungs and line the chest cavity (pleurae).
Originating in Central Asia despite widespread cultivation elsewhere, this is the most commonly grown species of a fuzzy-skinned stone fruit — what is its scientific name?
Prunus armeniaca is the most commonly cultivated apricot species.

Rooted in Minangkabau cooking, this dish slow-simmers meat in spiced coconut milk until the oil separates and it fries in its own glaze — both a method and a meal across the Malacca Strait; what is it?

Rendang is a fried meat or dry curry made of meat stewed in coconut milk and spices, widely popular across Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, and the southern parts of the Philippines, where each version is considered local cuisine.
First identified in Wuhan, this positive-sense single-stranded RNA virus prompted the WHO to declare a global health emergency from January 2020 to May 2023 — what's its name?
SARS-CoV-2 (SARSCoV2) is a coronavirus that causes COVID-19, the respiratory illness responsible for the COVID-19 pandemic that began in late 2019.
About 90% of the body's supply of this mood-regulating monoamine is actually made in the gut, where it helps drive intestinal movements — which neurotransmitter is it?
Serotonin (5-HT), is a monoamine neurotransmitter with a wide range of functions in both the central nervous system (CNS) and also peripheral tissues.

This genus of about 60 evergreen flowering plant species, native to the tropical Americas and Southeast Asia, is commonly grown as a houseplant valued for its large leaves and elegant white blooms — what genus is it?
Spathiphyllum is a genus of about 60 species of monocotyledonous flowering plants in the family Araceae, native to tropical regions of the Americas and southeastern Asia.
Educated in Rotterdam through World War II, this Indonesian economist later served as minister of finance, trade, and research under two different presidents — who was he?
Sumitro Djojohadikusumo (27 May 1917 - 9 March 2001) was an Indonesian statesman and one of the country's most influential economists.
Classed among the saurischians and placing them nearer to sauropodomorphs than to ornithischians, these hollow-boned, three-toed dinosaurs were ancestrally meat-eaters — which clade?
Theropoda (from ancient Greek -) is one of the three major clades of dinosaur, alongside Ornithischia and Sauropodomorpha.
Caused by the bacterium Francisella tularensis and treated with the antibiotic streptomycin, this tick-borne illness also goes by an animal-related nickname — what is it?
Tularemia is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Francisella tularensis.

This forceful expulsion of stomach contents through the mouth can result from food poisoning, pregnancy, motion sickness, or more serious causes like brain tumors, and is usually preceded by nausea — name this bodily reaction?
Vomiting (scientifically known as emesis, and otherwise known as puking, and throwing up) is the forceful expulsion of the contents of one's stomach through the mouth and sometimes the nose.
Each individual's coat is unique, and the best evidence suggests their black-and-white pattern wards off biting flies — which striped African equine is this?
Zebra (subgenus Hippotigris) are African equines with distinctive black-and-white striped coats.
This term for cancer that begins in gland cells applies to the most common form of breast cancer and one of the two major types of esophageal cancer — which term?
De Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter
Adenocarcinoma: Cancer of epithelial cells with glandular origin or characteristics.

Often called the greatest mathematician of the twentieth century, this German-born Frenchman revolutionized algebraic geometry before abruptly leaving his post at a Paris research institute in 1970 — who is he?
This memory disorder comes in two main forms — one blocking recall of events before a specific date, the other preventing new experiences from becoming lasting memories — what is it?
Amnesia: Cognitive disorder where memory is disturbed or lost.

Their larvae — nicknamed "doodlebugs" in North America for the marks they leave — dig sandy pits to trap passing ants, while the dusk-flying adults are often mistaken for dragonflies. What insect is this?
This American psychiatrist and pharmaceutical marketer amassed the world's largest personal collection of Chinese art, later donated to the Smithsonian — who is he?
Arthur M. Sackler: American physician and executive (1913–1987)
Nicknamed the hay bacterium for its soil habitat, this rod-shaped, spore-forming microbe is the best-studied Gram-positive species and a top industrial source of secreted enzymes — what is it?
Bacillus subtilis: Catalase-positive bacterium. It forms biofilms through the formation of extracellular polymeric matrix containing sugars and proteins.
This steroid medication treats everything from rheumatoid arthritis to psoriasis, and can even be given to speed a premature baby's lung development before birth — what is it?
Betamethasone: Steroid medication. It can be taken by mouth, injected into a muscle, or applied to the skin, typically in cream, lotion, or liquid forms.
A twinjet successor to a trijet predecessor, this American narrow-body airliner entered commercial service with Eastern Air Lines on New Year's Day 1983. Which aircraft?
Too small to fuse hydrogen but massive enough to briefly burn deuterium, these objects between 13 and 80 Jupiter masses cool over time through spectral classes M, L, T, and Y — what are they called?
With more than 220 species and over 26,000 registered cultivars, this flowering plant genus includes the very species whose leaves are processed into tea worldwide — which genus?
Camellia: Genus of flowering plants in the tea family.
A woody shrub native to South America, this starchy tuber yields tapioca and, when grated and toasted, becomes Brazil's farofa and West Africa's garri — what crop is it?
Cassava: Staple crop. Although a perennial plant, cassava is extensively cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions as an annual crop for its edible starchy tuberous root.
Also known as christophine or mirliton, this gourd-family fruit was first cultivated in Mesoamerica and is often cooked like summer squash — what is it?
Chayote: Edible fruiting vine of the gourd family.
Sold under the brand name Biaxin, this macrolide antibiotic treats everything from strep throat to H. pylori infections by slowing bacterial protein synthesis — what is it?
Clarithromycin: Antibiotic medication. Clarithromycin, sold under the brand name Biaxin among others, is an antibiotic used to treat various bacterial infections.
Widespread across Europe, Asia, and Africa, this small predatory falcon has occasionally strayed as far as Guam and the U.S. east coast — what bird is it?
Common kestrel: Species of bird. In the United Kingdom, where no other kestrel species commonly occurs, it is generally just called the "kestrel".
Nicknamed the jade plant or money plant, this low-maintenance South African succulent thrives on neglect and barely any water — what's its botanical name?
Crassula ovata: Species of succulent. It is sometimes referred to as the money tree; however, Pachira aquatica also has this nickname.
Designed to replace an earlier delta-wing jet for the French Air Force, this fourth-generation single-engine fighter first flew in March 1978 — which aircraft?
Dassault Mirage 2000: French jet fighter aircraft. Work on what would become the Mirage 2000 originated with the "Delta 1000" project launched in 1972.
In this heart condition, the heart chambers become enlarged and lose their ability to pump blood effectively, with causes ranging from genetics to alcohol and cocaine use — what is it called?
Dilated cardiomyopathy: Condition involving an enlarged, ineffective heart.

First imagined by Olaf Stapledon in his 1937 novel Star Maker and later named for a physicist who explored the idea in 1960, this hypothetical megastructure would encircle a star to harvest its energy — what is it?
Dyson sphere: Hypothetical megastructure around a star. A Dyson sphere is a hypothetical megastructure that encompasses a star and captures a large percentage of its power output.

In this lung disease the walls between the alveoli break down, merging tiny air sacs into enlarged spaces that shrink the surface available for gas exchange and starve the blood of oxygen. Which condition is it?
Emphysema: Chronic lung condition. Emphysema is a condition of the lung marked by abnormal enlargement of the alveoli with loss of pulmonary elasticity.
This Hungarian-American theoretical physicist won the 1963 Nobel for applying fundamental symmetry principles to the atomic nucleus and elementary particles — who was he?
Eugene Wigner: Hungarian-American physicist and mathematician (1902–1995)
This Stanford computer scientist built ImageNet, the vast labeled dataset that ignited the deep-learning revolution in computer vision in the 2010s. Who is she?

Passed down through generations rather than taught in a classroom, this field covers oral traditions like legends and proverbs as well as customs like festivals and traditional building styles — what is it called?
Folklore: Expressive culture shared by particular groups.
Once classified under two different bacterial genera, this nonmotile coccobacillus forms small gray colonies on chocolate agar and has its own colistin-oxolinic acid selective medium — which species?
Gardnerella vaginalis: Species of bacterium. Gardnerella vaginalis is a species of Gram-variable-staining facultative anaerobic bacteria.
Nicknamed creeping charlie and alehoof, this aromatic mint-family creeper is eaten as a salad green in some countries but reviled as an invasive lawn weed in North America — what plant is it?
Glechoma hederacea: Species of plant in the mint family. It is commonly known as ground-ivy, gill-over-the-ground, creeping charlie, alehoof, tunhoof, catsfoot, field balm, and run-away-robin.

Nicknamed for its mole-like digging forelegs and dense fur, this insect widespread across Europe and introduced to the eastern United States is a textbook example of convergent evolution — which species?
Gryllotalpa gryllotalpa: Species of cricket-like animal.
Native to North America, this genus of roughly 50 flowering plant species is better known by its common name — the sunflowers — and includes food crops for humans and livestock alike — which genus?

Helianthus: Genus of flowering plants, the sunflowers. Helianthus is a genus comprising around 50 species of annual and perennial flowering plants in the daisy family Asteraceae commonly known as sunflowers.
This extinct archaic human was the first to evolve a humanlike body and gait, the first to leave Africa for Asia and Europe, and the first to wield fire — who were they?
Homo erectus: Extinct species of archaic human. Homo erectus ( lit. 'upright man') is an extinct species of archaic human from the Pleistocene, spanning nearly 2 million years.
Distinct from a process that adds more cells, this one is an increase in the size of individual cells, like the uterus enlarging during pregnancy — what's it called?
Hypertrophy: Increase in the size of biological cells. Hypertrophy can lead to a relative increase in the volume of a tissue or organ, and contributes to the overall growth of an organism.
Besides NASA, Roscosmos, ESA and JAXA, the fifth partner agency running the space station belongs to which country?
The Canadian Space Agency is the fifth partner. China is not a partner at all -- it built its own station, Tiangong.
He won the Fields Medal in 1954 and, nearly half a century later, the very first Abel Prize in 2003 — which French mathematician of algebraic topology and geometry is it?

Conceived as a high-speed 'Schnellbomber' for the German Luftwaffe, this twin-engined WWII aircraft evolved into everything from a night fighter to the explosive lower half of composite 'Mistel' combinations — what is it?
Junkers Ju 88: German twin-engined multirole combat aircraft.
Situated between two larger folds of skin, these paired flaps extend from the inner vaginal and urethral openings and form the clitoral hood above — which structures are these?
Labia minora: Flaps of skin on either side of the vaginal opening in the vulva.
Cell signaling, homeostasis, metabolism, growth and reproduction are its hallmarks — and every instance of it eventually reaches death. What capacity in matter is this?

This Canadian physicist worked on the Manhattan Project determining critical mass values for uranium and plutonium, and in 1946 was fatally exposed to radiation in a lab accident at Los Alamos — who is he?
Louis Slotin: Canadian physicist and chemist (1910–1946)
In larger organizations it stacks into a pyramid, with a board and CEO at the top setting strategy — the broad practice of administering a business or government. What is it?
Management: Coordinating the efforts of persons.
Home to the heart, esophagus, trachea, thymus, and central chest lymph nodes, this compartment of the thoracic cavity sits between the lungs — what's it called?
Mediastinum: Central part of the thoracic cavity. The mediastinum (from Medieval Latin: mediastinus, lit. 'midway';pl.: mediastina) is the central compartment of the thoracic cavity.
This theoretical physicist and science communicator bridged science and science fiction well enough to win a 2021 lifetime achievement award named for Arthur C. Clarke — who is he?
Michio Kaku: American theoretical physicist, futurist and author.

There's a large introduced population of this small carnivorous mammal in Hawaii, though its family — split into the Herpestinae and Mungotinae — is native to southern Europe, Africa, and Asia — what animal is it?

Mongoose: Family of mammals in Africa and Asia. The Herpestinae comprises 23 living species that are native to southern Europe, Africa and Asia, whereas the Mungotinae comprises 11 species native to Africa.
Found in cardiac and skeletal muscle and distantly related to hemoglobin, high levels of this oxygen-storing protein let diving whales and seals hold their breath longer — which protein?
A vitamer of vitamin B3 that the body can build from tryptophan, in large prescription doses it lowers LDL and raises "good" HDL cholesterol — what's this compound also called niacin?
Nicotinic acid: Organic compound and a form of vitamin B3.
Native to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, this striped mammal looks like a zebra crossbred with a giraffe but is actually the giraffe's closest living relative — which animal?
Okapi: Species of mammal. Although the okapi has striped markings reminiscent of zebras, it is most closely related to the giraffe.

Produced in the hypothalamus and nicknamed for its role in love and social bonding, this peptide hormone also doubles as a pharmaceutical that speeds up childbirth by triggering uterine contractions — what is it?
Oxytocin: Peptide hormone and neuropeptide. Oxytocin is a peptide hormone and neuropeptide normally produced in the hypothalamus and released by the posterior pituitary.
Nicknamed "javelina" or "skunk pig," this social New World mammal travels in herds called squadrons and counts true pigs as its closest living relatives — what pig-like ungulate is it?

Nicknamed 'banana spiders' and 'armed spiders' for their aggressive posture, this genus found mainly in northern South America is better known by a name describing its roaming habits — what genus is this?
Home to cereal crops like wheat, rice, and maize as well as bamboo, this is the fifth-largest plant family on Earth — what is it called?
Poaceae: Family of flowering plants commonly known as grasses.
This beta blocker treats high blood pressure and performance anxiety alike, and can even shrink capillary hemangiomas in infants — what drug?
Propranolol: Beta blocker drug. It can be taken orally, rectally, or by intravenous injection.
First identified in the 1950s as a radio source, this extremely luminous galactic nucleus can outshine an entire galaxy like the Milky Way thousands of times over — what is it?
Quasar: Active galactic nucleus (AGN) containing a supermassive black hole.
Often compared to the film in a camera, this innermost, light-sensitive layer of the eye sends signals along the optic nerve to the visual cortex — what is it?
Retina: Part of the eye. The retina (from Latin rete 'net'; pl. retinae or retinas) is the innermost, light-sensitive layer of tissue of the eye.
Discovered in 1973 by Ruth Bishop via electron micrograph images, this fecal-oral pathogen is the leading cause of diarrheal illness in infants worldwide — which pathogen?
Rotavirus: Specific genus of RNA viruses.
Found in every ocean but never in fresh water, most of these bivalves can swim in rapid bursts across the seafloor rather than staying put — which shellfish?
Scallop: Family of shellfish, many edible.
This body of religious law, drawn from the Qur'an and hadith, refers to immutable divine law — distinct from fiqh, its human interpretation by scholars. What is it?
Sharia: Islamic law. Approaches to Sharia in the 21st century vary widely, and the role and mutability of Sharia in a changing world has become an increasingly debated topic in Islam.
A hygroscopic crystalline powder (formula NaNO2) and the most industrially important salt of its kind, this compound is most familiar to us cured into processed meats. What is it?
Sodium nitrite: Chemical compound. It is a white to slightly yellowish crystalline powder that is very soluble in water and is hygroscopic.
Famous for kite-shaped plates along its back and spikes on its tail, this Late Jurassic herbivore may have been preyed on by Allosaurus — which dinosaur?
Stegosaurus: Genus of Late Jurassic armored dinosaur.
Nicknamed 'knitbone' and 'boneset' for its traditional use in healing wounds, this perennial herb carries a liver-toxicity warning against internal use — which plant?
Symphytum officinale: Species of flowering plant in the borage family Boraginaceae.
The primary male sex hormone, this androgen builds muscle and bone, spurs body hair, and is even linked to mood, courtship display and dominance in both sexes — what is it?
Testosterone: Primary male sex hormone. It is associated with increased aggression, sex drive, dominance, courtship display, and a wide range of behavioral characteristics.

First identified in 1846 and nicknamed 'Peter Elam's disease' in parts of South Asia, this skin condition causing patchy discoloration is caused by an overgrowth of Malassezia yeast — what is it called?
Tinea versicolor: Skin disease. Tinea versicolor (also pityriasis versicolor) is a condition characterized by a skin eruption on the trunk and proximal extremities.
One of only a few fish able to keep its body warmer than the surrounding water, this fast-swimming ocean predator's yellowfin members can reach 75 km/h — what is it?
Tuna: Tribe of fish. Tuna (pl.: tunas or tuna) is a saltwater fish that belongs to the tribe Thunnini, a subgrouping of the Scombridae (mackerel) family.
This abnormal enlargement of veins in the scrotum is the most common correctable cause of male infertility, affecting around 15% of all men — what is it called?
Varicocele: Abnormal enlargement of the pampiniform plexus veins in the scrotum.

Also known as 'wet brain,' this neurological condition results from a severe thiamine deficiency and classically presents with confusion, poor coordination, and eye movement problems — which condition is it?
Wernicke encephalopathy: Medical condition. The condition is part of a larger group of thiamine deficiency disorders that includes beriberi, in all its forms, and alcoholic Korsakoff syndrome.
This Egyptian archaeologist twice served as his country's Minister of Tourism and Antiquities and has dug at sites from the Nile Delta to the Western Desert — who is he?
What is the chemical symbol for bromine?
The symbol for bromine is Br. Bromine is a chemical element; it has symbol Br and atomic number 35.
Tantalum is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for tantalum is Ta. Tantalum is a chemical element; it has symbol Ta and atomic number 73.
